visible_text: Compute \frac{\cos 60^\circ}{1-\cos(90^\circ-\theta)}+\frac{\cos 240^\circ}{1-\cos(270^\circ-\theta)}. Which of the following is equal to this expression? A: \frac{1}{\cos^2\theta}, B: \frac{\cos\theta}{\tan\theta}, C: \frac{\tan\theta}{\cos\theta}, D: \frac{1}{\cos\theta\tan\theta}
reasoning: Simplify cos60° = 1/2 and cos240° = -1/2. Use identities cos(90°-θ)=sinθ and cos(270°-θ) = -sinθ. The expression becomes (1/2)/(1- sinθ) - (1/2)/(1+ sinθ) = (1/2)[1/(1- sinθ) - 1/(1+ sinθ)] = (1/2)[2 sinθ / cos^2θ] = sinθ / cos^2θ = tanθ / cosθ, which matches choice C.
